review.summary: The proposal presents a study on comparing classical and neural rendering methods for creating photorealistic AI avatars. It outlines a clear motivation, research questions, and a structured methodology. However, there are several areas that require further clarification and detail to strengthen the proposal.

strengths.evidence_span: If the current development and adoption of AI and the Metaverse continues, holographic artificial intelligence assistants will likely be present in most of our lives.
strengths.reason: The motivation is timely and relevant, addressing a significant trend in technology.
strengths.recommendation: Continue to emphasize the importance of this research in the context of current technological advancements.

strengths.evidence_span: Main Research Question: How do state-of-the-art neural rendering methods compare to classical rendering approaches for real-time photorealistic AI avatars in terms of computational efficiency, visual realism, and implementation complexity?
strengths.reason: The main research question is well-defined and addresses a critical comparison in the field.
strengths.recommendation: Ensure that sub-research questions are equally clear and directly related to the main question.

strengths.evidence_span: The methodology will combine source research and quantitative methods.
strengths.reason: The proposal outlines a mixed-methods approach, which is appropriate for the research questions posed.
strengths.recommendation: Detail the quantitative methods to be used for clarity.

weaknesses.recommendation: Clearly define the target population and data sources to enhance the methodological rigor.

recommendations: Clarify the target population and data sources in the methodology section.

review.overall_assessment: The proposal is well-structured and addresses a relevant topic in the field of AI and rendering. However, it requires more detail in the methodology, evaluation, and limitations sections to strengthen its overall quality.

Motivation
If the current development and adoption of AI and the Metaverse continues, holographic artificial intelligence assistants will likely be present in most of our lives. They will need to be very natural to interact with, which means they also need to look natural for the interaction not to feel artificial.

One possible approach to achieve this is photorealistic avatars, which combine different domains like AI with computer graphics. These are however very difficult to create with current technology.
While we have been able to create near photorealistic humans for some time, adapting this progress to real-time rendering, necessary for AI assistants, has been a bigger challenge. If realistic avatars are imperfect, communicating with the assistant may always feel artificial, despite a perfect AI driving the conversation. This is due to the uncanny valley effectmori2012uncanny, where avatars that resemble humans, but fall short of full realism, can elicit discomfort.

Currently, there are many classical rendering methods for displaying the assistant and trying to climb out of the uncanny valley. However, one relatively new and promising area of research has been neural rendering, utilizing artificial neural networks to create images, which can appear more naturalShugao2021.

Approach

The last one is adaptability, which assesses how easy it is to implement and adapt the given method. We will evaluate how much experience is necessary for the implementation of the technique and how easily it is adapted to ones needs.
Evaluating and comparing these metrics allows one to robustly compare the different approaches and draw an accurate conclusion on which methods work best for each use case.
The methodology will combine source research and quantitative methods.

The first step will be to extensively research, analyze and evaluate the most relevant papers on neural rendering and classical rendering relevant to photorealistic avatars. This means we will focus mainly on papers by computer graphics and AI researchers(our target group). Presentations by developers, held during conferences like the Game Developers Conference, will also be relevant. Once we have an overview, we can select comparable methods on both sides. This allows us to apply the theoretical framework to directly compare the approaches.

After having chosen the methods, we will start with the implementation. 
For the approaches where the creation is based on real pictures, we will use DSLR cameras to capture a high-quality scan of a fellow student's head. For the more manual methods, we will try to match the look of the head to the already scanned head.

During this phase, we will take note of any difficulties that arise and will take note of the time it takes to implement. This allows us to better judge the adaptability of each method.
To test efficiency we will benchmark each method on the Lichtenberg Cluster. This means we will request the Hochschulrechenzentrum(HRZ) of the TU Darmstadt for access. We will use the latency in milliseconds as a unit for measurement.

After having gathered all the results in a single table in Microsoft Excel, we can move on to evaluate the realism. We will run the resulting image of each method through our implementation of the Structural Similarity Index measure in Python and compare each of them with a ground truth, which was already captured with the DSLR camera.
After this phase is over, we will go through each method and look at the efficiency, realism, and our notes on adaptability, which will allow us to then make a final evaluation and conclusion of each method.
